name: PageNora – Booking & Contact Page Monitor
author: PageNora

sections.description:
Small businesses lose customers quietly when the one page that brings in work breaks: the booking button disappears after a theme update, the contact form loses its fields, the quote page starts showing an error, or the page is accidentally hidden from search engines.

PageNora checks the pages you choose and emails you when something you approved on them goes missing, or when a page stops loading. This plugin connects your WordPress website to your PageNora account with one click and proves you own it, so you never copy a verification code by hand. Choosing the pages to watch then takes a few minutes in the PageNora dashboard.

What PageNora checks on the pages you choose (once a day on the free plan):

  • the page loads, and does not answer with an error;
  • wording you approved is still there;
  • buttons and links you approved are still there;
  • form fields you approved are still present;
  • the page is not set to be hidden from search engines.

What PageNora does not do: it never submits your forms, never makes bookings or appointments, never completes a checkout and never sends test messages through your contact form. A “looks right” result means the page still shows what you approved; it does not prove that a booking, order or message would go through.

The monitoring itself runs on PageNora’s servers. This plugin only connects your site and keeps PageNora’s verification tag on your homepage.

Requires a free PageNora account

The checks run on PageNora’s servers, so the plugin needs a PageNora account to work: signing in at app.pagenora.net with your email creates one. The free plan covers 1 website and 3 pages, checked daily, with no card needed and no end date. Paid plans are planned; no date has been set, you will be told before anything changes, and an account never becomes paid without your explicit enrollment.

External services

This plugin connects your website to PageNora, an external website-monitoring service at https://app.pagenora.net. The plugin needs it for everything it does: connecting the website to your PageNora account, getting the verification value that proves you control the website, and showing the status. The plugin itself does not monitor anything.

  • When: only after an administrator presses Connect to PageNora on Settings > PageNora. Nothing is sent before that, and nothing is sent when the plugin is only installed or activated.
  • What is sent on Connect: your browser opens PageNora with this website’s address, the address of this plugin’s settings page and a random one-time value. After you confirm on PageNora, the plugin sends back the one-time code PageNora gave, that random value and the same two addresses, and receives a key that works only for this website.
  • What is sent afterwards: the key, once a day (a WordPress scheduled task) and when an administrator opens Settings > PageNora or presses a button, to fetch the current verification value, ask PageNora to check it, show the status, or disconnect. WordPress’s standard request header includes your website’s address and WordPress version.
  • When the key stops working: Disconnect switches it off. PageNora also switches it off when the website is removed from your PageNora account, after Reset all settings or Sign out everywhere in PageNora, or after 30 days without use; the plugin learns this at its next request, deletes its stored connection, and Settings > PageNora asks you to press Connect again.
  • What PageNora reads: to verify, PageNora’s own servers read your homepage for the verification tag. To monitor, they read only the pages you choose in the PageNora dashboard.
  • Not sent: no visitor data, no user accounts, no form entries, no posts, no plugin list and no analytics. The plugin contains no tracking and no advertising and loads nothing from PageNora on your website’s pages.

The service is provided by PageNora.

  • Terms: https://pagenora.net/terms/
  • Privacy policy: https://pagenora.net/privacy/

What the plugin stores in WordPress

  • pagenora_connection: the key, the website name and when it was connected (not autoloaded).
  • pagenora_proof: the public verification value and when it expires. It is printed in your homepage’s head as <meta name="pagenora-verification" ...>, and stops being printed 14 days after it expires if it was never refreshed.
  • pagenora_revoked: a short note, kept at most 30 days, that PageNora switched this website’s connection off. Settings > PageNora shows it once, then deletes it.
  • A daily scheduled task that refreshes that value, and short-lived values (10 minutes or less) used during Connect.

Disconnect switches the key off at PageNora and then deletes all of these. If PageNora cannot be reached, nothing is deleted and the plugin asks you to press Disconnect again. Deleting the plugin asks PageNora to switch the key off and deletes what the plugin stored either way.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for PageNora, then press Install Now and Activate. (Or upload the plugin’s zip file with Upload Plugin on the same screen.)
  2. Go to Settings > PageNora and press Connect to PageNora.
  3. Sign in to PageNora if asked, check the website name and press Connect this website.
  4. You return to WordPress. PageNora reads your homepage for the verification tag, usually within a few minutes.
  5. Open the PageNora dashboard to choose the pages to watch.
sections.faq:
Does PageNora test-submit my contact or booking form?

No. PageNora checks that the page and the form’s fields are present. It never fills in or submits a form, never books and never buys anything.

How often are pages checked?

Once a day on the free plan. Paid plans with more frequent checks are planned; no date has been set.

Does the plugin slow my site down?

No. It adds one meta tag to your homepage. It loads no scripts or styles on your site.

What permissions does it need?

Only an administrator (the manage_options capability) can connect, check again or disconnect.

What if I remove the plugin?

Deleting it asks PageNora to switch the key off and removes everything it stored. If PageNora cannot be reached at that moment, the key is still deleted from your website; removing the website in your PageNora dashboard switches it off at PageNora too. Without the verification tag, PageNora pauses monitoring of that website after it notices the tag is gone.

Why does the plugin ask me to connect again?

PageNora switched off this website’s key. A key stops working when the website is removed from your PageNora account, after Reset all settings or Sign out everywhere in PageNora, or after 30 days without use (for example while the plugin was deactivated). The plugin then deletes its stored connection, and Settings > PageNora says so once. Press Connect to PageNora to connect again. More help: https://pagenora.net/help/wordpress-plugin/

Does it work with caching and page builders?

Yes. The tag is printed through WordPress’s standard wp_head hook, which themes, block themes and page builders such as Elementor, Divi and Beaver Builder all call. The verification value normally stays the same from day to day, so a cached homepage keeps working. If PageNora says the tag is missing, clear your page cache and press Check verification again. A homepage that does not come from WordPress at all (for example a separate landing-page service) cannot carry the tag.

What if WP-Cron does not run on my site?

WordPress runs scheduled tasks when someone visits the website. If the daily refresh is late, the tag keeps being printed for 14 days after the value’s expiry, and opening Settings > PageNora refreshes the value straight away and tells you the daily task was late. If your host has turned WP-Cron off, ask them to run it from a server cron.

Does it work on WordPress.com and on multisite?

On WordPress.com it works on plans that allow installing plugins. A WordPress.com site on a plan that does not allow plugins cannot install it; verify that site with one of PageNora’s other methods instead (the page title or the meta tag, both shown in the PageNora setup guide). On a multisite network each site connects separately, and deleting the plugin cleans up every site.

Where do I get help?

Read the help page at https://pagenora.net/help/wordpress-plugin/, use this plugin’s support forum at https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/pagenora/, or the contact form at https://pagenora.net/contact/. Settings > PageNora links to the help page and the forum too.
sections.changelog:
0.1.4

  • New display name: PageNora – Booking & Contact Page Monitor. The plugin’s address on WordPress.org, its folder and the Settings > PageNora menu stay the same.
  • When PageNora switches off this website’s connection (the website was removed from your PageNora account, Reset all settings or Sign out everywhere was used, or the connection was not used for 30 days), Settings > PageNora now says so once and asks you to press Connect again. Before, the page could go back to the Connect button without saying why.
  • Help and Support forum links on Settings > PageNora, and a Help link on the Plugins screen.
  • Removed the note that PageNora opens a limited number of new accounts each day.
  • The plugin’s web address now points to the WordPress plugin help page. New tags, a new FAQ entry, and new screenshots.
  • While PageNora is reading your homepage for the verification tag, Settings > PageNora says “Checking…” instead of showing an older result.
  • Sturdier connection handling: Disconnect removes the key here only after PageNora confirms it is switched off; an answer the plugin cannot read is shown as “could not read” instead of as numbers; a connection whose first verification request failed stays connected and offers Check verification again; the settings page waits less long when PageNora is slow.

0.1.3

  • The plugin’s web address now points to the PageNora help page, so it differs from the author’s web address, as WordPress.org requires.
  • The settings page now also says that the plugin contacts PageNora each time an administrator opens that page or presses one of its buttons.

0.1.2

  • A shorter settings page before connecting: one line and the Connect button first, with what Connect does and the account it needs in a section you can open.
  • Disconnect now asks you to confirm first and says what stops: the verification tag is removed and PageNora stops trusting this plugin’s key; the website stays in your PageNora account until you remove it there.
  • Right after connecting, the daily refresh says “Connected just now”.
  • Paused pages come with a short note and a dashboard link, and pages from a website you removed and connected again are no longer counted as paused.
  • PageNora’s Connect page names your website in its heading.

0.1.1

  • Disconnect now keeps your connection if PageNora cannot be reached, so you can try again instead of being left half disconnected.
  • The settings page counts only the pages that are switched on, and shows paused pages separately.
  • The sign-up wording matches the app: signing in creates a free account, and PageNora opens a limited number of new accounts each day.
  • Directory-ready readme, icons, banners and screenshots, and a repaired daily refresh task if WordPress lost it.

0.1.0

  • First version: connect with one click, verification tag, status, check again, disconnect, clean uninstall.

short_description: Get an email when your booking, contact or quote page loses a button, a form field or wording you rely on. One-click connection, no code to copy.
